Your side projects 60.8 as it stands, or 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. He is 0.3 clear of Salah and carries a reasonable ceiling—8% downside to two or fewer, but 25% upside to double figures.

The model wants Wood out for Watkins, a free transfer netting 6.4 points over the horizon. That takes you to 75.4 with Bench Boost applied this week, which is 3.6 better than using the chip later. Watkins replaces Wood in the starting XI; your armband decision remains unaffected.

You have three Arsenal and two each of Liverpool and Manchester City. The bench is thin—Mykolenko at 3.1 is the only real alternative—so whoever starts, starts.

Your team projects 69.0 with Haaland as captain—solid for the week. The suggested move swaps Wood for Watkins, gaining 6.4 points at no cost, which leaves you with a free transfer and £0.5m still in the bank. That's worth taking.

Bench Boost this week adds 14.2 points and outweighs waiting: your bench is thin (10.7 projected), so the timing matters. You're playing it in a week when it gains most relative to future options.

Three of your outfield players are Arsenal, two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. Haaland carries modest ceiling risk—8% chance of 2 or fewer—but is 0.3 clear of Salah in projection and remains the right captain choice. Salah's 7.9 would be the next call if that changes.

Make the Wood–Watkins swap, set Haaland as captain, play Boost, and you're ready.

Your team projects 69.0 with Haaland captained. The transfer gains 6.4 points net—Wood to Watkins costs nothing and is cleanly positive. Bench Boost this week is worth 14.2 points and genuinely the best week to play it, so that move stands. Those three decisions point the same way.

The weakness is concentration. Arsenal appear three times in your eleven, and Liverpool and Manchester City twice each. That is structural and not easily fixed without undoing sound individual picks—Salah and Haaland are your top two, and Saka and Gabriel belong in the squad. It is not a reason to move now, but it is what to watch.

Haaland carries the armband with a 0.3-point lead over Salah. That margin is tight enough that either could outperform the other in a single week, but the model backs him. He has an 8% tail of scoring 2 or fewer, against which his 25% chance of 10+ offers real upside.

The Bench Boost into Watkins plus your bench (10.7 projected) gives a clean single-week spike. After the transfer, you have £0.5m unspent and one free transfer in the bank. That leaves you well-placed to respond if something breaks, though not to chase many options.
